messages:
Prateek: Quick sync — we need to decide on "staged swapback" semantics for A/B canaries. Proposal: controller emits an explicit fallback decision, router applies it with a configurable 'swapback window' that can either immediate-switch or 'dribble' traffic back to stable over N seconds. Questions: cache invalidation, session affinity, decision API surface, and private-deploy compatibility.

Maria: +1 on explicit decisions. Two immediate concerns: (1) KV/prefix cache invalidation when we swap back (we can avoid full purge by tag-based selective eviction), (2) session affinity — mobile clients with sticky sessions will see mid-response model changes.

Kevin: For cache evictions I like tag-based eviction too. For swaps, suggest a 'dribble' mode: step traffic back in small pct increments, e.g., 10% every 30s, to avoid thundering and let caches warm on the stable path.

Ashley: From SRE/runbook perspective we need a deterministic failure mode. Add metadata on the decision: rollout_id, action, reason, decision_ts, ttl. Also we should default to fail-open for non-critical reads and fail-closed for any write/payment endpoints.

Jon: Interface boundary suggestion: router subscribes to a Decision API (gRPC or message bus) and applies instructions with these fields: rollout_id, action, target_variant, method (immediate|dribble), params, reason. Sample payload: 
```json
{
  "rollout_id": "r-2025-04-12-14",
  "action": "fallback",
  "target": "stable-v42",
  "method": "dribble",
  "params": {"duration_s": 120, "step_pct": 10},
  "reason": "p95>200ms"
}
```
This keeps router logic thin. Controller decides and emits.

Maria: +1 to keep router dumb. One small tweak: include optional 'session_persist": true/false' flag so router knows whether to honor existing session affinity on partial dribble.

Prateek: Good point. Also think about private deployments that don't run our controller. We need a portability layer: either a lightweight controller binary they run, or a Kafka topic + schema that on-prem teams can push decisions to. Router should support both subscription modes.

Kevin: For portability, emitting decisions to a topic `rollout.decisions.v1` works. Router can be configured with a consumer. That avoids gRPC firewall issues in customer networks.

Ashley: Telemetry: decisions should be tagged in metrics/traces (rollout_id, variant, decision_reason). Add rollbacks to audit log automatically. Also update oncall playbook to include 'inspect decision + inspect dribble progress' steps.

Jon: Edge case: what if new variant is misrouted mid-response (lambda long-poll)? We need to ensure per-request routing is resolved strongly at request start. Router must resolve route & cache decision for request lifetime.

Prateek: Agreed — router must snapshot decision per request. Also we need TTL on decisions so expired decisions don't linger.

Maria: Implementation thoughts: RFC should cover 1) Decision schema, 2) Router application semantics (snapshot, dribble algorithm), 3) Cache eviction API/contract (tagging + selective invalidation), 4) Private deployment compatibility.

Kevin: POC idea: implement dribble algorithm in router as token-bucket style where tokens map to slots allocated to new/stable variant, step controlled by decision.params. Quick perf test will show p95 oscillation.

Ashley: Ops action: add rollout_id to all alerting dashboards and escape hatch in console to force immediate swapback. Also annotate who triggered rollout in audit.

rollout-bot: NOTE: canary-controller v0.9 deployed to staging at 2025-04-12T14:02Z — emits decision topic to `rollout.decisions.v1`.

Prateek: Next steps: Maria to draft RFC (decision schema + router contract), Kevin to spike dribble POC in router, Ashley to update runbook checklist. I'll own the portability section (topic + sample consumer). Can we sync on RFC draft by EOW? :calendar:

Maria: I'll have a first draft by Thursday EOD.

Kevin: POC started, will post logs here.

Ashley: I'll update the playbook skeleton and share a PR.

Prateek: Thanks — if anyone objects to the decision-driven model speak now. Otherwise I'll collect notes into RFC template and @-mention owners. :thumbsup:
